thread:
marie_support: forwarding a customer repro — ACME gets 400 on toolcall when args include percent signs and appears to cut off (Invalid JSON: unexpected token '%').

marie_support: customer says they ran this from Windows cmd:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/toolcall ^
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME123" ^
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" ^
  -d "{\"tool\":\"pdf_extractor\",\"args\":\"[\\\"C:\\Users\\Carlos\\Invoices\\invoice%20final.pdf\\\",\\\"page\\\":1]\"}"
```

jess_s: thanks — can you ask them to paste the raw body from a capture (postman/mitm) if possible? the curl above has escaping inside cmd, looks hairy.

marie_support: pasted the body from their server logs (raw bytes):
```
{\"tool\":\"pdf_extractor\",\"args\":\"[\\\"C:\\Users\\Carlos\\Invoices\\invoice%20final.pdf\\\",\\\"page\\\":1]\"}
```

jess_s: aha — two things: 1) Their args field is a string that contains a JSON array. 2) In cmd.exe a single % can trigger environment variable expansion (like %USERNAME%) which can mutate the payload before curl sends it. If cmd expanded something it could remove a trailing quote or bracket and produce the parser error.

sam_eng: we reproduced locally on Windows cmd by running the same curl. If the filename contains `%20` it's fine, but if it has an unpaired `%VAR%` or a lone `%` cmd strips it. Repro steps:
```
C:\> set MYVAR=
C:\> curl -d "{\"tool\":\"t\",\"args\":\"[\\\"C:\\path\\file%notvar.pdf\\\"]\"}" http://localhost:8080/toolcall
# Windows cmd expands %notvar% -> empty, resulting in: ...file.pdf\\\"]\\\"} (closing bracket may be missing)
```

sam_eng: on our side the parser throws: 400 Invalid JSON at char 42: unexpected token '%'.

jess_s: suggested quick workarounds for customer:
- Use PowerShell with single-quoted JSON payload (no % expansion)
- Escape % by doubling it: use `%%` in cmd (e.g., invoice%%20.pdf)
- Use the Redwood SDK or --data-binary to avoid cmd quoting changes

marie_support: told customer to retry with doubled percent (%%) or run in PowerShell and to paste a raw capture if it still fails. They asked for a more permanent fix on our end.

sam_eng: filing bug to make parser validation clearer and to surface original raw bytes in logs for support. Filed BUG-12345 and attached repro steps + Windows cmd note.

infra-bot: BUG-12345 created by sam_eng — title: "toolcall: malformed args from cmd.exe percent-expansion leads to JSON parse error". Priority: P2.

ops_lead: can we consider adding a detection rule: if args is a string that looks like a JSON array, run a secondary parse and if that fails, log both the outer and inner raw bytes and a hint about shell expansion? would reduce back-and-forth.

sam_eng: agreed. I'll add a validation hint and include mitigation docs for Windows shell gotchas.

marie_support: replied to customer with the two workarounds and that we're tracking a bug; customer will try the PowerShell option and update.

marie_support: closing loop here — will reopen if customer still fails. :thumbsup:
